answers: Doctor: When did the walking difficulty start, and has it been rapidly worsening, slowly progressing, or stable? Patient: I haven’t noticed any walking trouble; mostly I’ve just felt apathetic and been more focused on cravings like chocolate pudding and potato chips.

Doctor: Have you noticed any new weakness, numbness, or trouble with balance in your legs (eg, needing to catch yourself or stumbling)? Patient: No—I haven’t really noticed any numbness or leg weakness, and I haven’t been stumbling or needing to catch myself. I mostly feel detached and preoccupied with cravings, though.
I haven’t noticed any specific thigh or hip weakness when climbing stairs. It’s more that I feel detached and distracted, and I’m focused on certain cravings rather than how my legs feel.
“No, I haven’t noticed any involuntary jerking or twitching, and I’m not having any worsening trouble speaking or swallowing—I just tend to feel detached and keep thinking about certain foods.”

Doctor: Have you or anyone noticed any changes in your speech, such as slurring or difficulty finding words, or any confusion/behavior changes besides food cravings? Patient: No slurring or word-finding trouble that I’m aware of, but people say I’ve been acting inappropriately and seem less interested in family interactions—though I don’t really see it the same way.

“No—my memory and thinking speed feel about the same to me, and I mostly notice that I’ve felt detached, less engaged with family, and preoccupied with cravings. Other people call it personality changes, but I don’t experience it as anything beyond being focused on food and acting differently.”

“No, I haven’t noticed any involuntary writhing or jerking of my face, hands, or trunk, and I’m not aware of any worsening movements when I’m at rest. Mostly it’s just that I feel detached and preoccupied with cravings.”

“No, I haven’t noticed any jerky facial or hand movements—no grimacing or tapping that I’m aware of. My thinking hasn’t clearly declined either; I mostly feel detached and preoccupied with cravings, and other people comment that my behavior is inappropriate.”
“No—no one in my family has been diagnosed with a movement disorder or a progressive mental or behavioral decline, at least not that I’m aware of.”

Doctor: Have you noticed any involuntary jerking, fidgeting, or irregular facial/hand movements that worsen when you’re stressed or trying to stay still? Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any jerking or fidgeting—mostly I just feel detached, and my attention keeps going back to cravings.
